chunks: And from him, from a number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Dawud ibn al-Nu'man, from Abu Ayyub al-Kazzaz, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'Tell me about Al-Aqiq. Is it a miqat (station of consecration) that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) designated, or is it something the people did?' He said: 'Indeed, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) designated Dhul Hulaifah for the people of Medina, and he designated Al-Juhfah for the people of the Maghreb (West), and it is recorded with us as Mahya'ah. And he designated Yalamlam for the people of Yemen, and he designated Qaran al-Manazil for the people of Ta'if, and he designated Al-Aqiq for the people of Najd, and whatever is from Najd.'

key_terms.الْجُحْفَة: Al-Juhfah, the miqat for the people of the Maghreb (West)
key_terms.الْعَقِيق: Al-Aqiq, a valley and miqat station near Medina, designated for the people of Najd
key_terms.ذَا الْحُلَيْفَةِ: Dhul Hulaifah, the miqat for the people of Medina
key_terms.قَرََنَ الْمَنَازِلِ: Qaran al-Manazil, the miqat for the people of Ta'if
key_terms.مَوَاقِيت: Miqat, the stations of consecration for Hajj
key_terms.يَلَمْلَمَ: Yalamlam, the miqat for the people of Yemen

ai.seo_question: What is the designated miqat for the people of Najd according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* explicitly lists the miqat stations assigned by the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) for various regions, confirming Al-Aqiq as the designated miqat for the people of Najd. It establishes these locations as prophetic ordinances rather than mere local customs, providing a clear geographical framework for the ritual of Ihram. The narration also notes the alternative name 'May'ah' for Al-Juhfah, reflecting the scholarly attention to geographical nomenclature in Shia jurisprudence.
